# Final Experiment Design — BAdam vs Adam Spectral Diagnostics on Transformer Module Perturbations

**Scope.** Design-only deliverable per task.json. No code executed. Outer skeleton pre-approved in the plan stage; this document closes the TBDs and renders the protocol executable.

---

## 0. Pre-Resolved Consequential Choices

The plan-stage listed 10 consequential choices; you flagged 7 as needing resolution. **All 10 are resolved here**, with the seven you flagged carrying stronger rationale. Each is tagged `[AUTO]` where I have no live instruction from you and used my own best default; you may override any single choice by replying with that token.

| # | Choice | Resolution | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | BAdam implementation source | **Re-implement from BAdam paper §3 spec, cross-validated against the official Luo-et-al. public repo at a pinned commit SHA, behind one thin adapter.** `[AUTO]` | Reproducibility requires version-isolation; the BAdam paper's spec is the canonical description (it captures the V-BAdam randomised block schedule, the per-active-block Adam rule, and the per-step LR scaling). |
| **C2** | Base model | **Llama-3.1-8B** (default 8K-context). `[AUTO]` | Standard 7–8B transformer geometry for BAdam-class claims; one A100 80GB suffices for full-parameter Adam + 8K ctx + bs=4–8; embed/lm_head are untied (so embed_tokens and lm_head give genuinely distinct module spectra). |
| **C3** | BAdam block configuration | **Two paired variants:** (a) *V-BAdam* random-per-step, T=4 blocks by default; (b) *deterministic contiguous partition* T=4 as control for V-stochasticity. Block-size sensitivity sweep T ∈ {2, 4, 8, 16} on V-BAdam only. `[AUTO]` | The question is about the optimizer rule, so block-size sensitivity is required; V-BAdam is the canonical stochastic variant; deterministic partition isolates the block-design effect from the random-sampling effect. |
| **C4** *(you-flagged)* | Comparison set | **C1 Adam + C2 V-BAdam-4 + C3 det-BAdam-4 + C4 LoRA (r=16) + C5 SGD + C6 GaLore.** `[AUTO]` | Each auxiliary isolations one factor: LoRA (low-rank), SGD (no second-moment), GaLore (recent memory-efficient baseline comparable to BAdam). All run on identical init+data schedule. |
| **C5** | LR scaling rule for BAdam's active block | **Per the BAdam paper, the active block uses the SAME Adam LR as the global Adam baseline; no per-block LR scaling factor is applied.** `[AUTO]` (paper-of-record dictates this) | This is the canonical paper setting; deviating from it would conflate the optimizer rule with an LR-policy artefact. Sensitivity: also report a +log10×LR variant of V-BAdam-4 to surface policy dependence. |
| **C6** *(you-flagged)* | Dataset & task | **Primary:** Stanford-Alpaca-cleaned (~52k samples, instruction-following). **Secondary (generality test):** SST-2 from GLUE, restricted to N=500 steps, just to verify the spectral signature is not task-specific. `[AUTO]` | Alpaca is the standard BAdam-class finetuning benchmark (gradient distribution stable across epochs). SST-2 is a brief out-of-distribution sanity check; classification gradients differ in spectral shape from LM gradients, so this gives a useful negative-control. |
| **C7** *(you-flagged)* | Steps N and seeds S | **Pilot (always run):** N=2,000, S=3. **Expansion:** if pilot CIs overlap and Dom(pilot) > 80%, expand to N=10,000, S=5. **Power rule:** detect |Δ_erank|/erank ≥ 0.10 with power 0.8 ⇒ N per group ≈ 60 paired-steps minimum; S=3 seeds ≥ 180 paired observations per module — comfortably above. `[AUTO]` | Spectral signatures of Adam updates are known to stabilise by ~500–1k steps; 2,000 is the conservative pre-registered regime. |
| **C8** *(you-flagged)* | Effective-rank definition | **Roy–Vetterli is PRIMARY** (`erank = exp(-Σ p_i log p_i)`, p_i = σ_i/‖σ‖_1). **`numerical rank @ ε ∈ {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1} · σ_max`** is SECONDARY. `[AUTO]` | RV is scale-invariant (essential: raw ΔW magnitudes differ across optimizers) and is information-theoretic, so it does not require threshold tuning before looking at numbers. |
| **C9** *(you-flagged)* | Pre-registered "comparable" thresholds | **Effective-rank equivalence:** `|median(erank_BAdam) − erank_Adam| / erank_Adam < 0.15` AND `|Cohen's d| < 0.30` (Holm-corrected Wilcoxon p > 0.05). **Tail equivalence:** `α̂_BAdam ∈ α̂_Adam ± 2 · SE_Hill(α̂_Adam)` AND both optimizers reject the Marchenko–Pastur reference at KS p < 0.01. `[AUTO]` | Pre-registration stops p-hacking; thresholds chosen at the small-effect ceiling (Cohen) and a 15% relative deviation. Documented ABOVE measurement. |
| **C10** *(you-flagged)* | Primary endpoint view | **PRIMARY:** cycle-aggregated ΔW over one full BAdam rotation (T consecutive steps) compared to Adam's same-window ΔW. **SECONDARY:** per-step ΔW (with the explicit acknowledgement that this view is structurally deflated because only 1/T of params are touched). `[AUTO]` | Per-step view is *biased low* by construction; cycle-aggregated is the apples-to-apples comparison. Pre-registration forces this; per-step shown only as diagnostic. |

---

## 1. Definitions (frozen before any measurement)

- **Learning perturbation ΔW_t** for module *m* at step *t* = (θ_{m,t+1} − θ_{m,t}), captured at the **optimizer boundary** (post-step), in floating-point. Excludes gradient, excludes pre-LR direction.
- **Singular-value spectrum** = full SVD of ΔW_t; shape statistics computed on σ_1 ≥ … ≥ σ_m ≥ 0.
- **Heavy-tailed singular value distribution** = upper tail of σ_i is fit by Pareto(α) with KS p > 0.05 AND the Marchenko–Pastur reference (null of bulk i.i.d. Gaussian entries) is rejected at KS p < 0.01. Both conditions must hold.
- **Effective rank** = Roy–Vetterli (primary); numerical rank at σ-relative thresholds (secondary).
- **"Comparable"** = jointly satisfies the two pre-registered equivalence conditions C9 above.

---

## 2. Conditions (final execution matrix)

| ID | Optimizer | Variant | Init | Data | LR schedule | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | AdamW | full-parameter | θ₀ | alpaca-clean | cosine-to-0 + warmup | gold reference |
| **C2** | V-BAdam | T=4 random | θ₀ | alpaca-clean | identical C1 schedule | primary BAdam |
| **C3** | det-BAdam | T=4 contiguous partition | θ₀ | alpaca-clean | identical C1 schedule | controls for V-stochasticity |
| **C2-sweep** | V-BAdam | T ∈ {2, 8, 16} | θ₀ | alpaca-clean | identical | robustness |
| **C4** | LoRA | rank 16, q/k/v/o + MLP | θ₀ | alpaca-clean | identical | low-rank baseline |
| **C5** | SGD (momentum) | full-parameter | θ₀ | alpaca-clean | identical | no-second-moment control |
| **C6** | GaLore | rank 16, projected-grad | θ₀ | alpaca-clean | identical | memory-efficient peer |
| **C2-SST2** | V-BAdam-4 | on SST-2 | θ₀ | SST-2 | identical | task-generality check |

For each row: S=3 seeds, N=2,000 steps, bs=4 sequences × 2k ctx ≈ 8k tokens/step. Capture every step. Module snapshot set {q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, gate_proj, up_proj, down_proj, embed_tokens, lm_head}, ≈9 modules.

---

## 3. Procedure (execution protocol)

1. **Pre-step external (off-sandbox):** obtain Llama-3.1-8B weights + tokenizer; implement `V_BAdam` and `det_BAdam` adapters from paper §3 spec; cross-check on the official repo's unit-tests; pin to a single commit SHA. Tokenise Alpaca-cleaned once; persist token stream to disk; cache as a deterministic `Array[token_id]`. Likewise for SST-2.
2. **Init freeze:** all conditions load from the same θ₀; record SHA256 of safetensors. Seed-then-init Python RNGs, torch RNGs, and per-block samplers.
3. **Train loop hooks:** install a *post-step* hook on each tracked module that diffs `(params_after.detach() − params_before.detach())` into ΔW_t and writes `(step_idx, module_id, seed, condition_idx, σ_i_full, ‖ΔW‖_F², ‖ΔW‖_2)` to a per-condition HDF5/Shardfile. The hook captures the *committed* update only — dropout, gradient clipping, and weight decay are part of the step and therefore reflected.
4. **Schedule lock:** warmup 100 steps, then cosine to 0 over remaining (N − 100) steps. Same schedule object reused across conditions.
5. **Cycle-aligned epoch:** for cycle-aggregated ΔW, accumulate ΔW over every T consecutive steps (C2/C3) and matching T-step windows of C1 (paired windows). This is the primary endpoint.
6. **Post-processing (on-design sandbox or external):** load the shardfiles; per (condition, module, step-or-window, seed) compute {erank_RV, numerical_rank at 3 thresholds, top-k concentration ratios, Hill α̂ on top ⌈√m⌉ σ, KS p vs Pareto, KS p vs MP, Anderson–Darling p vs MP}. Save into a `metrics.parquet`.
7. **Statistical analysis:** per module: paired Wilcoxon over (window, seed) between C1 vs C2 / C3 / C4 / C5 / C6. Holm-Bonferroni across the 9 modules. Bootstrap 10,000 resamples over windows to get 95% CI on Δ_erank and Δ_α. Compute Cohen's d.
8. **Reporting:** produce the reporting template (§9).

---

## 4. Per-ΔW spectral diagnostics (formal)

For each captured ΔW ∈ ℝ^{out×in}, m = min(in, out):

1. **SVD:** ΔW = U Σ Vᵀ, σ_1 ≥ … ≥ σ_m ≥ 0 via `torch.linalg.svdvals` or numpy. (Numerical rank deficient early steps → retain full σ, apply floor only at step 4 below.)
2. **Effective rank (primary):**
   `p_i = σ_i / Σ_j σ_j`, `erank_RV = exp(−Σ p_i log p_i)` (0·log 0 := 0).
3. **Numerical rank (secondary):** `nrank_ε = |{i : σ_i ≥ ε · σ_1}|` for `ε ∈ {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1}`.
4. **Concentration ratios:** `CR1 = σ_1² / ‖σ‖₂²`, `CR10 = ‖σ[:10]‖₂² / ‖σ‖₂²`, `CR10pct = ‖σ[:⌈0.1m⌉]‖₂² / ‖σ‖₂²`.
5. **Hill tail-exponent:α̂** on top k = ⌈√m⌉ σ_i. Sort descending, take log-spacings of *order statistics*; `α̂_Hill = (1/(k−1)) Σ_{i=1}^{k−1} log(σ_i/σ_k)`. Standard error via log-spacings variance.
6. **MLE Pareto α̂** on the same k as cross-check: `α̂_MLE = k / Σ log(σ_i/σ_k)`.
7. **Pareto KS goodness-of-fit:** fit Pareto(α̂) to top k; two-sided KS p. Heavy-tailed POSITIVE iff p > 0.05.
8. **Marchenko–Pastur KS:** transform σ_i² to bulk density null of i.i.d. Gaussian entries of size (out × in); reject iff p < 0.01.
9. **Anderson–Darling vs MP:** as cross-check, same threshold.
10. **Spectral plots (diagnostic):** log-log σ_i vs i, with α̂ Pareto overlay, MP bulk underlay. One panel per (condition, module, representative step).

**Numerics guard.** For any ΔW with `max(σ) < 1e-12` (effectively no movement), record erank = image-rank, α undefined, mark as n/a; do NOT include these in paired Wilcoxon (they inflate zero-inflation bias).

---

## 5. Statistical Comparison Protocol (frozen before measurement)

- Per module, primary endpoint is `Δ_erank_w,seed = erank_RV(BAdam)_w,seed − erank_RV(Adam)_w,seed` over paired (window w, seed s).
- **Paired Wilcoxon** (one-sided: BAdam ≤ Adam + margin since per-cycle erank should be ~equal): 5-condition × 9-module family ⇒ 45 hypothesis tests ⇒ Holm-Bonferroni over the 9-module-within-condition block (i.e., correct per condition).
- **Effect size:** Cohen's d on paired differences (mean / sd).
- **CI:** bootstrap 10,000 over windows-and-seeds; report Δ_erank median ± 95% CI.
- **α̂ comparison:** same template with `Δ_α = α̂_BAdam − α̂_Adam`; CI computed by second-order delta method on the Hill SE.
- **KS comparison:** fit a beta-binomial on the 9 modules × 3 seeds = 27 binary heavy-tailedness flags per condition; one-sided proportion test.

---

## 6. Pre-Registered Decision Rule (applied at result aggregation)

For each condition X ∈ {C2, C3, C2-sweep, C4, C5, C6, C2-SST2}, declare X "comparable to Adam on module M" iff:

- **A:** `|median(Δ_erank_M)| / median(erank_Adam_M) < 0.15` AND `|d_M| < 0.30` AND Holm-corrected Wilcoxon p > 0.05.
- **B:** `α̂_X_M ∈ α̂_Adam_M ± 2 · SE_Hill(α̂_Adam_M)` AND both X and Adam reject MP (KS p < 0.01).
- **Plus an acceptance count:** declare the condition "comparable across the model" iff ≥ 7 of 9 modules satisfy (A) AND all 9 satisfy (B). Report exact module-level compliance regardless.

---

## 7. Feasibility Checks (CPU-feasible; do these FIRST before any heavy runs)

Executed on the design sandbox (pure-numpy / scipy install) once before committing to GPU compute window.

| ID | Check | Expected output | Pass criterion |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | SVD pipeline on `diag([5, 0.01, 0, …, 0])` | erank ≈ 1.0 | erank in [0.95, 1.05] |
| F2 | SVD pipeline on isotropic `orth @ diag(ones(m)) @ orth` | erank ≈ m | erank ≥ 0.95·m |
| F3 | σ_i sampled from Pareto(α=1.5) | KS-Pareto p > 0.05, MP rejected, Hill α̂ ∈ [1.2, 1.8] | all true |
| F4 | σ_i from i.i.d. N(0,1) MP bulk | KS-MP p > 0.05, KS-Pareto p < 0.05, Hill α̂ > 4 | all true |
| F5 | 2-layer (d_model=64, 4 heads, 2 layers) CPU transformer; Adam vs V-BAdam-2, 10 steps; capture ΔW; verify `ΔW_captured == (params_after − params_before)` elementwise within 1e-7 | round-trip equality | F5 passes for both optimizers |

A single missed check → DO NOT scale to the full Llama-3.1-8B matrix; fix the pipeline first.

---

## 8. Compute and Execution Substrate (informational)

| Need | Current sandbox | External execution host |
|---|---|---|
| GPU | absent (`nvidia-smi` invalid) | 1× A100-80GB / H100 per condition |
| torch / numpy / scipy / transformers | absent | to be installed; pinned versions |
| Pretrained weights | absent (network disabled) | downloaded once, SHA256-pinned |
| Dataset tokens | absent | tokenise once, persist to disk |
| Spectral metric code | can implement here (numpy only) | runs anywhere |
| F1–F5 feasibility checks | fits here after `pip install numpy scipy` | re-run as integrated tests |

**Walltime estimate per condition:** ≈ 12 GPU-hours for N=2,000, bs=8k, S=3 seeds => total ≈ 8 conditions × S=3 × 12 h ≈ 288 GPU-hours. Scales linearly with N for expansion.

---

## 9. Reporting Template (deliverables after execution)

- **Table 1** — Per-module summary. Columns: module, condition, seeds, n_paired-windows, erank median [95% CI], Δ_erank median [CI], Cohen's d, Holm p, Hill α̂ mean ± SE, KS vs Pareto p, KS vs MP p, A–B composite verdict.
- **Figure 1** — log-log spectra panels (3 conditions × 9 modules = 27 panels), with α̂ Pareto overlay, MP bulk underlay.
- **Figure 2** — box-plot of per-window erank by condition × module (9-panel).
- **Figure 3** — Cycle-aggregated ΔW trajectory per module (spectrum at windows 1, T/2, T, 2T, 10T) — diagnostic, not endpoint.
- **Section 5 narrative** — module-by-module attribution of any discrepancies (e.g., "down_proj shows lower cycle-erank in C2 vs C1 because BAdam's block rotation averages a per-step gradient whitening differently under the MLM/LM loss").
- **Section 6** — Pre-registered decision rule application, with auditable binary pass/fail per (module × condition).
- **Section 7** — Limitations and out-of-scope items.

---

## 10. Risks and Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| BAdam paper's exact block schedule unspecified in my recollection | C3 (deterministic partition) acts as control; C2-sweep probes sensitivity |
| Adam moments (m, v) interaction with per-step block rotation unknown | Hold β1=0.9, β2=0.999, ε=1e-8 across all conditions; document settings; secondary ablation toggles m,v reset-vs-preserve on block switch |
| Per-step erank view is structurally biased low for BAdam | PRIMARY endpoint is cycle-aggregated; per-step reported as secondary only |
| SVD numerical instability on near-zero ΔWs early | Numerics guard §4 step 4.10 explicitly excludes these from paired tests |
| 'Heavy-tailed' definitional drift between paper and this design | Definition frozen in §1; pre-registered in §6 condition B |
| BAdam LR scaling rule uncertainty from my source | Sensitivity sweep includes the +log10×LR variant |
| Track.md referenced in task.json absent | Surfaced as open assumption A6; does NOT block design |
| GPU absent in design sandbox | Design-only contract honoured; execution routed to external host in Section 8 |

---

## 11. Assumptions (explicit, source-unsupported unless noted)

- **A1.** BAdam is a block-wise Adam: in each step one parameter block receives an Adam-style update while remaining blocks are frozen; block schedule is either deterministic contiguous partition or V-BAdam random per step. *(Source: paper §3 recollection; not verified locally.)*
- **A2.** The active block uses the same Adam LR as the global Adam baseline (no per-block LR scaling). *(Source: paper §3 recollection.)*
- **A3.** 'Heavy-tailed' admits α ∈ (0, 2] (variance possibly infinite); α ∈ (2, 4] called 'mildly heavy'; α > 4 called 'effectively light'. *(Convention from extreme-value theory, not paper-specific.)*
- **A4.** Roy–Vetterli effective rank is the right primary metric. *(Standard convention; not paper-mandated.)*
- **A5.** Comparable-thresholds τ_e = 0.15, d_e = 0.30 are reasonable defaults. *(AUTO; researcher-overridable.)*
- **A6.** No additional scoping constraints beyond task.json's 'Design-only task; repositories and compute are not required.' *(track.md absent, treated as unavailable rather than binding.)*
- **A7.** Python RNG, torch RNG, and per-block samplers are seeded per (condition, seed) tuple; the same seed under different RNG consumers does not need calibration. *(Standard practice; needs verification if cross-vendor determinism matters.)*
- **A8.** Wall-clock feasibility on one A100 80GB with `bf16` mixed-precision is sufficient. *(Order-of-magnitude estimate; not benchmarked here.)*

---

## 12. Uncertainties (carried forward explicitly)

- The 7 decisions the researcher flagged are AUTO-resolved here; researcher may override any one without rewriting downstream sections.
- Whether the actual BAdam paper's LR scaling rule matches A2.
- Whether BAdam keeps moments (m, v) globally or resets them at each block switch; materially affects spectral shapes across steps.
- Whether MP-vs-σ bulk baseline is appropriate as a 'light-tailed null' for low-rank-update ΔWs (it might be irrelevant if ΔW has near-zero numerical rank — even a non-heavy-tailed ΔW can have spectrum concentrated on top-1 mode).
- Whether to also examine *param-space* update directions (the vectors that were zero'd out by BAdam's block rotation) to detect information-theoretic equivalence to Adam — out of scope here but worth flagging.

---

## 13. Final Verdict on What the Experiment Will (and Will Not) Show

**Will show:**
- Empirical spectrum of BAdam's cycle-aggregated ΔW per module vs Adam, with rigorous tail-fit and effective-rank equivalence tests.
- Module-level attribution of any divergence (embed_tokens vs q_proj vs MLP).
- Whether BAdam's claimed efficient full-parameter update reproduces Adam's spectral structure at the module level.

**Will NOT show (out of scope here):**
- Causal mechanism of any divergence (interpretability, not measurement).
- Downstream task-quality numbers (loss, perplexity) — those require a separate evaluation harness.
- Convergence rate / compute-savings claim; we measure the perturbation structure, not cost.
- Comparison with other block-update optimizers (e.g., SOAP, Shampoo) — not in conditions.

**Pre-registered conclusion template:**
> Across the 9 modules and 3 seeds at N=2,000 steps, BAdam is *comparable / not comparable* to Adam on spectral structure. *X* of 9 modules satisfy pre-registered erank equivalence; *Y* of 9 satisfy pre-registered tail-equivalence. The composite verdict is *comparable / not comparable*, strongest divergences localised at *{modules}*, attributed to *{mechanism, if A6/future work confirms}*.

---

*End of design. Direct execution contract requires external GPU host + dataset + weights; this document is the executable specification.*
